# qAOP Predictor

Quantitative adverse outcome pathway (qAOP) models of **cisplatin-induced kidney
injury**, served as a JSON API and a web UI at https://qaop.vhp4safety.nl.

Machine-readable contract: /openapi.yaml (or /openapi.json). Browsable: /docs.
Use **/api/v1**. The unversioned /api/* routes are deprecated and frozen for an
existing consumer.

## Start here

    GET  /api/v1/models      capabilities, accepted AND calibrated ranges, endpoint definitions
    GET  /api/v1/ranges      accepted and calibrated parameter ranges
    POST /api/v1/predict     run the model
    GET  /api/v1/health      liveness

    curl -X POST https://qaop.vhp4safety.nl/api/v1/predict \
      -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
      -d '{"model_type":"invivo","dose":5,"time":672}'

Inputs are only `model_type` ("invitro" or "invivo"), `dose`, `time` and an
optional `simulation_count` (1-1000, default 250). Anything else is ignored.

## What this service is NOT

It cannot answer, and must not be used to answer:

- human or patient risk
- any chemical other than cisplatin
- repeated, chronic or multi-cycle dosing
- a benchmark dose, BMD, BMDL, NOAEL or any point of departure
- whether a dose is safe
- kidney function, creatinine or eGFR
- in vitro to in vivo extrapolation
- any species other than RPTEC/TERT1 cells and rat

This is a research model. It is not a clinical, patient or regulatory
risk-assessment tool.

## The two models are separate

`invitro` is RPTEC/TERT1 renal proximal tubule epithelial cells in culture,
dosed in **uM**. `invivo` is rat kidney after a single intravenous dose, in
**mg/kg**. Nothing converts between them and the service performs no in vitro
to in vivo extrapolation. Confusing the units silently produces a valid-looking
answer to a different question.

## What the endpoints actually are

`dna_damage` -- eigengene score of TXG-MAPr WGCNA module rKID:160 (p53 target
genes), in arbitrary units, computed from log2 fold-change against control. A
transcriptomic surrogate, **not** a measured DNA lesion level, concentration or
cell count. Peaks and then decays.

`necrosis` -- **two different measurements under one key.** In vitro: the
*fraction* (not percentage) of propidium-iodide-positive cells, capped at a
sampled parameter whose posterior runs 0.700-0.998 (median 0.767), so the in
vitro model structurally **cannot** predict total cell death. In vivo:
expert-graded H&E necrosis severity on a 0-1 ordinal scale. **Do not compare or
average the two.**

`inflammation` (in vivo only) -- eigengene score of module rKID:7m (NF-kB target
genes), roughly 0-8 on the calibration scale. A transcriptomic surrogate.

`kidney_failure` (in vivo only) -- expert-graded **interstitial fibrosis
severity**, mapped onto 0-1 in increasing order of severity. The source figure
for this state variable is titled "Fibrosis"; the AOP diagram box reads "Kidney
Failure". It is **not** acute kidney injury, **not** eGFR or creatinine,
**not** loss of kidney function and **not** a probability of renal failure. It
is cumulative and never decreases, so a longer simulated time mechanically
increases it, and its asymptote depends on dose.

## Reading a result

`final_value` is the value **at the time you asked for** -- not a peak, not a
steady state. Because endpoints behave differently in time (kidney failure
accumulates; the others peak and decay), changing `time` moves them in opposite
directions. Compare runs only at the same `time`.

**The percentile band is not a prediction interval.** `percentile_2_5` and
`percentile_97_5` are percentiles of the Monte Carlo ensemble over
pre-calibrated posterior parameter draws. They exclude observation and residual
error, between-animal and between-replicate variability, model-structure
uncertainty, and **all in vivo pharmacokinetic uncertainty** (the PK rate
constants and scale factor are hard-coded, and their omitted uncertainty is
larger than the band shows). The band is pointwise over the time grid, not a
simultaneous band over trajectories, and in the in vivo fit it is narrower than
the spread of the data it was fitted to. **A narrow band does not mean the
prediction is accurate.**

**Results are stochastic and there is no seed.** Repeated identical
250-iteration requests differ by a few percent. Do not quote more than **two
significant figures**, and do not read a small run-to-run difference as a
signal. `min` and `max` are sample extrema, not bounds.

**Very small values are numerical artefacts.** The Hill exponents are large
(roughly 18-38), so far below the calibrated dose range the output falls orders
of magnitude below anything the calibrating assays could detect. A necrosis
value of 1e-23 does not mean "a little necrosis"; it means the model is outside
the region where it carries information.

## Calibrated versus accepted

The accepted input ranges are **much wider** than the data the models were
fitted to, and the service will not fail loudly outside them: both kinetic
subsystems are linear in dose, with dose entering only through the initial
conditions, so an out-of-range dose produces output that looks exactly as
well-behaved as a calibrated one.

| | accepted | calibrated |
|---|---|---|
| invitro dose | 0.001-150 uM | 0.1-50 uM |
| invitro time | 0.1-168 h | to 72 h |
| invivo dose | 0.1-10 mg/kg | 1-7.5 mg/kg |
| invivo time | 1-2160 h | to 672 h |

Narrower still, and the single most important caveat for the in vivo model:
**the histopathology endpoints (`necrosis`, `kidney_failure`) were scored at one
dose only -- 5 mg/kg**, 12 time points to 672 h, 3 rats per point. Every in vivo
necrosis or fibrosis number at any other dose is extrapolation with no
supporting histopathology. In vivo dose-response data at 1/2.5/5/7.5 mg/kg exist
for transcriptomics and kinetics only.

For `invitro` necrosis: PI-positive cells were absent below 50 uM and early
(<20 h) data were discarded, so below 50 uM the value is a switch output rather
than a measurement-backed prediction. At the top of the accepted range the
output is essentially the fitted saturation constant: 100 uM and 150 uM differ
in the fourth decimal place, so the model has no dose resolution there.

`/api/v1/predict` reports all of this per request in `warnings[]`, with codes
`dose_outside_calibration`, `time_outside_calibration`,
`histopathology_extrapolated`, `below_detection_threshold`,
`uncertainty_band_degenerate` and `monte_carlo_noise`. **An empty `warnings`
array is the only case in which the request sits inside the calibrated domain.**
`simulation_count=1` is accepted and produces a zero-width band shaped exactly
like a real one; use the default of 250 or more for anything quantitative.

## Errors

Every /api/v1 error is `{"error": {"code", "message", "details"}}`. Branch on
`code`, never on `message`. Codes: `invalid_request`, `unknown_model`,
`parameter_out_of_range`, `malformed_json`, `unsupported_media_type`,
`not_found`, `method_not_allowed`, `prediction_failed`, `service_unavailable`.
A 4xx means fix the request; only `prediction_failed` and
`service_unavailable` are server-side.

## Not established by this service

Do not assert these; they could not be settled from the code and data shipped
here, and the API deliberately does not claim them:

- the exact mapping of the five histopathology categories
  (Absent/Minimal/Mild/Moderate/Marked) onto 0-1
- whether the in vitro and in vivo `dna_damage` arbitrary units are on the same
  scale -- treat them as **not** numerically comparable
- the physical units of the in vivo pharmacokinetic states
- whether the posterior draw files are post-warmup, post-thinning, converged
  samples; no per-parameter convergence diagnostics ship with the service, so
  the band cannot be described as a verified posterior-propagation band

## Provenance

Model and calibration: Toxicological Sciences, doi:10.1093/toxsci/kfaf177
(PMID 41514178). Posterior draws: `draws_cisDDNEC2024-08-05` (in vitro),
`draws_cisvivo2024-08-07` (in vivo). The `version` reported by the API is the
**application** version and says nothing about the model calibration.

Source: https://github.com/VHP4Safety/qAOP-app
